Before archive/currentization and before blocked shutdown/claim-release or later executable-model work resumes, Daniel Vicory must independently review and explicitly approve the final migration and verification packet. This Bead is intentionally blocked until `dwv-o2g.8` is complete.

## Stop rule
Do not archive or sync the migration, delete temporary correspondence/aliases, close the migration campaign, or release downstream dependencies before approval is recorded here. Rejection returns the required repair to the relevant migration or verification Bead.

A final review is required because terminology and semantic-ID changes can look mechanically equivalent while altering canonical ownership, reviewed-state meaning, persisted-format behavior, or model claim boundaries. - **Trust the automated checks and archive immediately:** rejected because tools cannot decide whether a product-facing distinction was compressed or whether a compatibility decision is acceptable.
- **Review only the design:** rejected because implementation, generated projections, trace formats, and historical cleanup can diverge after approval.
- **Require operator approval for every downstream Bead:** rejected because one final authority decision with a complete packet is clearer and less brittle.

title: Separate portable operation driving from physical execution
description: Implement the missing portable product execution seam so one admitted operation can remain owned across semantic authority waits, physical submission, delayed completion, normalized result delivery, and reconciliation. Preserve the current transaction, operation-slot, store, recovery, LifecycleRelease, and CodedRangeClean authority boundaries. A simple blocking implementation must remain valid.
design:
Current canonical requirements already define the needed correctness; this is implementation architecture, not a new semantic owner or a requirement to name “sans-I/O.” Reuse TransactionMachine next_action/apply, OperationAdmission/OperationSlotTable, StoreCompletion, RecoveryCommitObservation, ReleaseAuthorization, and the accepted non-terminal CodedRangeClean outcomes.

Keep one service-owned operation-driver record per exact OperationSlotToken. It owns the transaction machine and operation-local plan/working state. The operation slot remains the sole owner of the canonical request, frontend buffer/resource tokens, child identities, submitted state, completion evidence, drain, and reconciliation state. Bind each child to its exact physical descriptor before submission: operation generation and child index, store identity/incarnation, operation/range, ordering/durability intent, and a buffer lease or owned resource whose lifetime reaches terminal disposition.

Separate executor acceptance from completion. Record each child as reserved, accepted, or terminal. Accepted physical work remains owned until exact completion, conservative reconciliation, or durable recovery handoff. A role-neutral executor reports a delivery envelope carrying the exact store identity/incarnation with the existing normalized StoreCompletion; service fan-in validates exact operation generation, child, store incarnation, identity, and order, aggregates required child results, and supplies only normalized ActionResult observations to transaction and other semantic owners. Reconciliation consumes real executor/backend or recovery observations, not terminal dispositions fabricated from cached slot state. Keep recovery-state commit through its separate typed RecoveryCommitObservation port rather than inventing a generic effects framework.

A bounded service scheduler owns runnable/waiting bookkeeping. Record coded admission contention and admitted-but-capture-blocked effect permission as distinct pending reasons. Contention holds no coded claim and re-runs admission when relevant owner state changes; capture blocking retains the admitted claim and rechecks effect permission without re-admission. Neither state performs dependent member I/O while blocked. Claim/capture/resource/completion changes trigger bounded reconsideration; no wait queue, wakeup selection, retry, or fairness policy moves into coded/CLEAN semantics. Frontend abandonment only removes delivery interest. Cancellation is an executor input and never proves rollback.

The blocking/file implementation may accept work, execute it immediately, and deliver the completion in the same outer drive turn, but it must traverse the same submission and observation boundary. Do not select Tokio, io_uring, ublk transport, batching, one-task-per-request, Datalog, or a general effect system here.
acceptance_criteria: Focused implementation and review establish all of the following without changing product semantics: (1) exact generation- and store-incarnation-qualified submission/completion correlation rejects stale, wrong-store, or otherwise mismatched delivery without mutating a current operation; (2) one operation supports multiple physical children with delayed and out-of-order completion, safe terminal duplicates, and fan-in only after every required child has an exact disposition; (3) pre-acceptance refusal is distinguished from accepted work, and submission, completion, and durability are never conflated; (4) short, failed, uncertain, duplicate, and late results flow through existing normalized owner observations, while reconciliation consumes real executor/backend or recovery observations rather than cached slot state fabricated as terminal evidence; (5) operation-driver, slot, buffers, coded authority, basis observations, and child resources remain owned until terminal/reconciled disposition or durable handoff; (6) frontend abandonment suppresses delivery without discarding or rolling back owned work; (7) coded admission contention and capture exclusion are distinct retained pending reasons: contention holds no claim and re-runs admission, capture blocking retains the admitted claim and rechecks effect permission; neither performs dependent I/O while blocked, and each can make progress after its matching owner-state change; (8) a deterministic fake executor can delay, reorder, fail, duplicate, make uncertain, misroute across stores, and selectively complete children; (9) the existing blocking/file path implements the same boundary with immediate completion; and (10) fresh read-only architecture review finds no synchronous call/return, scheduler policy, duplicated ownership, runtime choice, Linux transport assumption, or task-4.2 shortcut left correctness-bearing. Only after this review gate may CodedRangeClean task 4.2 resume.

description: HealthyPortableService::finish() performs consequential terminalization: it snapshots child operations, synthesizes uncertain outcomes when requested, records reconciliation, and reclaims operation resources. title: Investigate Linux ublk batch I/O transport boundary
description: Determine whether Linux ublk batch I/O provides a materially stronger and more maintainable completion-evidence boundary for DiskWeave than the traditional COMMIT_AND_FETCH protocol, and recommend whether DiskWeave should adopt it. This is an investigation and recommendation only: it authorizes no implementation, transport switch, OpenSpec change, or acceptance claim.
design: Inspect current canonical OpenSpecs and active changes before recommending any semantic work. Compare traditional and batch transport using the pinned libublk source, kernel/API documentation, and bounded repository evidence. Establish whether batch I/O separates fetch lifecycle from completion acknowledgement; what kernel and libublk guarantees it supplies; whether operation, tag, and trace ownership can remain held until explicit transport completion acknowledgement or reconciliation; how partial commit, commit failure, quiesce/fetch cancellation, and shutdown with outstanding commits behave; which kernel-version and libublk constraints apply; and whether the model is materially simpler. Do not encode Linux API names as product requirements. Map any candidate stable rule to its existing canonical owner. Report a genuine semantic gap only if current authority does not already own the authority required before operation ownership release.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an evidence-backed recommendation choosing exactly one outcome: adopt batch I/O; retain the traditional protocol with a justified stable contract; or investigate another alternative. The report must address clean shutdown, outstanding commits, partial commit, commit failure, quiesce or fetch cancellation, completion evidence, ownership release, kernel support constraints, unreleased libublk dependencies, and implementation maintainability. State whether the result is only a Linux adapter decision or exposes a missing stable DiskWeave semantic. If an actual semantic gap exists, identify the missing behavior, explain why current authority does not own it, name the existing capability/change that should receive clarification if one exists, or justify why a new OpenSpec change would be needed. If adoption is recommended, identify only the smallest coherent follow-up implementation/spec work; do not pre-author speculative OpenSpec changes.
notes: This investigation is the explicit prerequisite for dwv-3wo. Before resuming the production Linux shutdown candidate or investing further in the traditional-protocol adversarial harness, decide whether batch I/O should replace the transport seam that created the completion ambiguity. Keep this issue OPEN and parked until explicitly started. It is separate from dwv-hg0's portable-shutdown work; do not create a dependency on portable shutdown, endpoint withdrawal, and claim-release ordering without independent repository authority.
close_reason: Investigation completed: adopt Linux ublk batch I/O as the dwv-3wo transport direction; existing canonical semantics already own the required completion/ownership rules.

comments.author: Daniel Vicory
comments.text:
Decision recorded from external investigation on 2026-08-27: adopt Linux `UBLK_F_BATCH_IO` for the `dwv-3wo` production transport repair rather than extending the traditional combined `COMMIT_AND_FETCH` completion/fetch evidence model.

Basis: the Linux batch UAPI separates request fetch from completion commit and defines partial commit as only the kernel-reported handled prefix; failure handles none. Current upstream libublk-rs has a dedicated batch queue transport with internal commit IDs, partial-commit resubmission, fetch-stop handling, and shutdown drain. This materially removes the traditional protocol's fetch-cancellation/completion ambiguity.

This is a Linux adapter decision, not a new portable DiskWeave semantic. Existing canonical owners already require operation/tag/buffer ownership to remain until safe terminal or reconciliation evidence and forbid converting unknown/ambiguous effects into success. No new OpenSpec change is required merely for the transport switch.

Implementation caveat for `dwv-3wo`: transport submission is not kernel acknowledgement. Current upstream libublk batch code drops its own fetched-tag ownership at commit submission while tracking commit acknowledgement internally, so DiskWeave must establish an exact acknowledgement/reconciliation boundary before releasing its generational operation resources. Partial commit, commit failure, and tag reuse are review-sensitive.

External references captured 2026-08-27: Linux ublk docs `https://docs.kernel.org/block/ublk.html`; Linux UAPI `https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h`; upstream libublk batch source `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ublk-org/libublk-rs/main/src/io_batch.rs`.

title: Linux ublk acceptance hangs during clean shutdown
description:
## Problem
`./tools/linux-disk-acceptance/run.sh` does not complete after the production `dwv start` publication check. The guest script sends SIGTERM and waits for the frontend, but the process remains alive until forcibly killed.

## Reproduction
1. Start the existing `dwv-linux-acceptance` Lima VM.
2. Run `./tools/linux-disk-acceptance/run.sh` from the repository.
3. Observe that the release build completes, `/dev/ublkb0` is published, and the command then exceeds the harness timeout instead of producing `results/evidence.json`.

Observed twice:
- Linux `7.0.0-29-generic`: timed out after 900 seconds.
- Linux `7.0.0-28-generic` selected with one-shot GRUB reboot: timed out after 600 seconds.

The second run was stopped with SIGKILL after inspection. Guest cleanup removed the workload and `/dev/ublkb0` was absent.

## Evidence
The guest process tree at timeout was `guest.sh -> ./target/release/dwv start --array ... --json`. After SIGTERM, the main `dwv` thread remained sleeping in `futex(..., FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET, ...)`, consistent with `libublk::UblkCtrl::run_target` waiting to join queue threads after the device callback returned. A queue worker repeatedly entered `io_uring_enter(11, 0, 0, IORING_ENTER_EXT_ARG, ... timespec 20s)` and returned 0; it did not exit. No request workload was needed to reproduce the hang: the first production publication phase stops the server before filesystem I/O.

The frontend installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that only set `STOP_REQUESTED`; normal-context cleanup calls `running.stop_dev()` before `run_target` joins queue handlers. The likely trigger is an idle ublk queue with no completion event to mark the queue stopping after STOP_DEV. This is an evidence-based hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

## Scope and non-claims
This blocks live Linux/Lima acceptance evidence for the trace-retention change. It does not establish that the trace-retention implementation caused the hang; the changed trace path is not exercised before the first publication stop. Do not replace clean shutdown with a force-kill workaround or claim the acceptance passed without the generated evidence artifact.
design:
`dwv-y97` selected batch ublk I/O as the production direction. Repair this bug at the Linux frontend/transport boundary using `UBLK_F_BATCH_IO` or the current maintainable libublk abstraction over it; do not extend the traditional `COMMIT_AND_FETCH` classifier as the default path.

Preserve existing canonical ownership and uncertainty semantics. Queuing a completion to userspace/libublk is not kernel acknowledgement. A generation-bearing DiskWeave operation, frontend tag, buffer, and related resource ownership may be released only when the exact completion is supported by the batch commit acknowledgement contract or by an existing conservative reconciliation outcome. Handle partial commit only for the kernel-reported handled prefix; failure or unknown delivery must not manufacture completion, release, or safe tag reuse.

Keep signal handling async-safe and keep transport shutdown bounded. The implementation agent owns the concrete libublk revision/API adaptation, queue/event-loop design, batching policy, deterministic test structure, and acceptance VM kernel. Updating the disposable VM kernel is allowed. Prefer the smallest maintainable dependency/API change that exposes the evidence DiskWeave needs; a larger libublk shim or direct-UAPI implementation is allowed only as a reviewable candidate, not as an unreviewed correctness shortcut.

The parked quiesce candidate and adversarial harness are historical evidence/scaffolding, not required implementation ancestry. Work from the current live tree and reconcile concurrent frontend changes rather than restoring those revisions wholesale.
acceptance_criteria:
- The supported acceptance VM actually advertises the batch ublk capability used by the implementation; upgrading that disposable VM kernel is allowed. The evidence records the tested kernel and relevant ublk feature/protocol choice.
- Idle/no-I/O SIGTERM exits normally within the bounded acceptance runtime: admission/fetching stops, queue workers join, the owned endpoint is removed, and no SIGKILL/manual cleanup is needed.
- Shutdown with admitted/in-flight I/O is exercised so the fix is not only an idle wakeup. The exact operation/tag/buffer ownership remains held until acknowledged completion or conservative reconciliation.
- Focused deterministic evidence covers successful acknowledgement, partial commit, commit failure/unknown handling, and generation-safe tag reuse; no submission-only or fetch-cancellation signal is accepted as completion proof.
- The complete Linux acceptance script produces and validates `results/evidence.json` and leaves no owned `/dev/ublkb0` endpoint or workload process behind.
- The external completion-evidence review child created for this track approves the final acknowledgement/release boundary; any blocking delta is applied and the final acceptance is rerun before `dwv-3wo` closes.
- Closure claims the transport/shutdown bug and its completion-ownership boundary only. It does not silently claim completion of broader portable clean-shutdown semantics that this acceptance did not exercise.
notes:
Observed 2026-08-15 in /Users/daniel.vicory/src/DiskWeave. VM: dwv-linux-acceptance (Lima VZ, aarch64, 4 CPUs, 8 GiB). Kernel 7.0.0-29-generic timed out at 900s after VM reset; one-shot GRUB boot into 7.0.0-28-generic timed out at 600s. Main-thread strace showed futex wait; queue-thread strace showed repeated io_uring_enter with a 20-second timeout returning 0. SIGKILL cleared the process and device; no acceptance result was produced.
PARKED HANDOFF (2026-08-15):

Confirmed defect: traditional Linux ublk idle shutdown can hang indefinitely; dwv start can remain alive joining an idle queue after SIGTERM. This was observed during Linux acceptance. No force-kill acceptance claim is valid.

Production candidate, unfinished: jj change nrpzkqrlsnrxqyrwkymomwylpwqtwpmo / commit 91380bd0471f5359d69163322b396529945ac621 (Fix idle Linux ublk shutdown). It pins an unreleased libublk revision exposing quiesce_dev(), enables UBLK_F_QUIESCE | UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY, and uses quiesce as a candidate idle-queue unwind mechanism. Host cargo check -p dwv-frontend-ublk passed; guest cargo test -p dwv-frontend-ublk --lib --no-run passed. The current frontend test suite is not fully green because of the reported saturation-retirement assertion. The exact current production revision has not completed Linux runtime acceptance on 7.0.0-28 or 7.0.0-29; older acceptance evidence is not validation of this revision.

Known correctness problem: quiesce failure followed by successful kill_dev leaves QUEUE_FAILED false. A later QueueIsDown can therefore satisfy the completion classifier and be treated as proof of the preceding combined completion/fetch operation. Successful forced stopping does not independently establish completion. Do not fix during parking.

Traditional transport issue: COMMIT_AND_FETCH combines completion and next-fetch behavior. It remains unresolved whether DiskWeave should rely on fetch-side abort ordering as evidence about a preceding completion. The new batch-I/O investigation dwv-y97 is the prerequisite decision before resuming this production candidate or the traditional-protocol harness.

Adversarial experiment, unfinished: jj change wskwoyntwspkplvuouzoysytwlrkknrs / commit ff31e317e137b254d3fd02f74ecd6237caff46f0 (Add Linux ublk quiesce-boundary proof harness), child of the production candidate. The latest real-kernel test did not complete: only QuiesceBeforeCommit began, the controlled write never reached before-commit, cleanup/join timed out, and CommitBeforeQuiesce never ran. completion_proven derives from the production classifier and is circular; client success/error does not independently prove delivery; commit-submitted does not prove the controlled command was submitted-but-not-completed; the earlier report of committed O_DIRECT|O_SYNC usage was inaccurate. Keep the revision as experimental scaffolding; it is not accepted evidence.

Retained durable nodes may compose into larger durable integrity roots/groupings. Finer volatile CV/subtree material is reconstructible acceleration. Configurability does not imply arbitrary byte sizes: supported geometry may be restricted by hash/tree alignment and construction.

Provide an array-level default with optional override at stable semantic ChecksumTarget identity: data SlotId or parity/Q coding position under the applicable topology. Replacement StoreId, assignment instance, or physical media does not implicitly change integrity policy. Physical-device cache sizing, concurrency, prefetch, and similar tuning remain outside durable integrity semantics unless a later decision proves a physical property is required to interpret evidence.

Checksum evidence must be bound, directly or through immutable/versioned checksum-set and profile identity, to the exact effective checksum semantics under which it was created. Later mutable configuration inheritance cannot reinterpret it; records need not duplicate a complete resolved profile when set/profile identity supplies the same independently inspectable invariant. Classify every selected parameter as semantic/durable or reconstructible/performance-only.

Require online incremental/background and opportunistic construction, safe interruption/restart, and preservation of old valid evidence until coherent activation retires it. Start from coherent activation rather than range-progressive authority; reconcile array- versus member-level activation against current complete-active-set semantics. Do not introduce arbitrary range-local active-profile mosaics without compelling evidence. Resolve whether cached CVs may contribute to newly durable evidence and what freshness, corruption, and validation model makes that safe. Keep supplemental recovery-code geometry independent and avoid SQLite layout as semantic architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture and evidence may iterate in parallel, but closure requires sufficient reproducible evidence for consequential geometry, durability, activation, and trust choices. The outcome defines retained durable node/localization and larger root/grouping semantics, volatile cache non-semantics where applicable, stable ChecksumTarget override identity, effective-profile binding, supported size/alignment rules, online migration/restart, coherent activation domain, historical interpretation, cache trust, and large-member scaling. Reconcile the selection against current OpenSpec; update OpenSpec only where product/correctness behavior changes or a canonical semantic gap is filled; record consequential non-semantic architecture durably. Create or retain explicit production implementation work before closure. Selected consequential behavior may not live only in a report.
